title: Routing rules
intro: One list, read from the top. The first rule a call matches decides who answers it — the rest are never reached. Order is the whole logic.
action_human_note: Rings the business handsets. The assistant never picks up.
action_blocked_note: Hung up before it rings. No recording, no transcript.
action_agent_note: Answered, transcribed, and acted on by the named assistant.
rule_spam_note: Updated daily from the community list. Nothing is recorded.
rule_emergency_note: Rings every handset at once, day or night.
rule_reception_note: Falls through to the assistant when nobody picks up within 20 seconds.
rule_afterhours_note: Takes messages and offers appointment slots.
rule_prefix_note: Switched off after it blocked a customer last week.
fallback_title: Everything the list did not match
fallback_note: This rule cannot be deleted or moved — it is what makes sure no call is left unanswered.
try_empty: With no rules in the list there is nothing to walk. Every number, known or not, falls through to Rezeption Wagner.
trace_1: 1 Known spam list — not on the list
trace_2: 2 Withheld numbers — the number is visible
trace_3: 3 Staff and owners — not a saved number
trace_4: 4 Emergency contacts — not in that group
trace_5: 5 Reception hours — it is 09:41 on a Thursday
empty_title: No rules yet — every call goes to the assistant
empty_body: That is a working setup, not a broken one. Add a rule when something needs to bypass the assistant: the doctors’ own numbers ringing straight through, or a number that keeps calling and should be blocked.
offline_title: Phone line offline — no rules are being applied
offline_body_before: Changes you make here are saved, but nothing will route until registration to
dialog_subtitle: A condition, what happens when it matches, and where it sits in the list.
cond_number_hint: Several numbers, comma separated. Matched exactly.
cond_number_say: a call comes from a saved number
cond_prefix_hint: Everything starting with this. Wide by nature — check it does not catch customers.
cond_prefix_say: the number starts with that prefix
cond_group_hint: Stays current on its own as contacts move in and out of the group.
cond_group_say: the caller is in that group
cond_hours_hint: Read in Europe/Vienna, and it follows your closures.
cond_hours_say: the call arrives inside that window
cond_anon_hint: No number is sent at all — nothing else about the caller is known.
choice_human_note: Rings the business handsets. The assistant never picks up. Falls through after 20 seconds if nobody answers.
choice_blocked_note: Hung up before it rings. No recording, no transcript, nothing in the archive.
choice_agent_note: Answered, transcribed and acted on by the assistant you name.
pos_top_say: at the top, before every other rule
pos_bottom_say: at the bottom, after every other rule
warn_bottom: At the bottom, rules 1 to 8 are checked first — anything they already match will never reach this one. Move it up if it is meant to be an exception.
warn_prefix: A prefix matches everything that starts with it. Rule 8 was switched off for exactly this reason after it blocked a customer.
plain_blocked: the call is hung up before it rings
error_title: The rules file on disk is not valid
error_body_after: but stopped reading it at line 24 — a rule is missing its match pattern. Until it parses, the last working set of rules stays active, so calls are still being routed correctly.
result_body: Rule 5, Reception hours, matches first — the call rings a person. Rules 6 to 8 are never checked, and neither is the fallback.
try_footer: Nothing is dialled. This only replays the list against the number.
